questions: Trace durable state under power loss, quota pauses, stale leases and cancellation.
Preserve product files and Plan 2 inputs while deleting only verified control artifacts.
decision: Harden crash recovery and cleanup around ownership, process identity and durable receipts; retain the file-backed lifecycle instead of introducing a distributed workflow service.
code_observations: lifecyclectl uses an active pointer and runner lease to prevent duplicate execution, recover interrupted tasks and guard cleanup.
The reusable project resource map is outside disposable plan directories. The former Plan2-input exception is no longer needed, but prepared research is still a retained project artifact.
implementation_steps: Use PID plus process-start identity and host identity when deciding whether a local lease is live. Treat uncertain remote leases conservatively.
Add fault-injection tests around claim, checkpoint, atomic replacement and lease release; ensure recovery never fabricates validation or completion.
Keep cancel/reset scoped to recognized plan roots and registered jobs. Never run an indiscriminate git clean/reset or remove product source/tests.
Pin successful validation receipts to the source/command/map state that produced them; reuse a receipt only if those inputs still match.
Preserve prepared reports outside disposable controls and retain incomplete plan state on failure. Document portable relocation rather than asking users to edit task status manually.
proposed_acceptance_tests: A reused PID does not authorize killing an unrelated process.
Interruptions after each state-write boundary retain completed subtasks and recover only in-progress state.
Symlinks, parent paths and directories without the plan sentinel cannot be cleaned.
Cancelled jobs are stopped before their control directory is removed.
Successful cleanup preserves implementation, tests, shared resource inventory and research reports.

alternatives.title: Trust a PID or delete the whole work root
alternatives.tradeoff: Low code cost, unacceptable risk to unrelated work and ambiguous recovery.

alternatives.title: Owned leases and pinned receipts with fault injection
alternatives.tradeoff: Uses existing architecture and buys verifiable recovery at low runtime cost.

alternatives.title: Replace the runner with Temporal/LangGraph now
alternatives.tradeoff: Durability concepts are useful, but framework migration adds services/dependencies without demonstrated need.

cost_model: Favor deterministic checkpoint reuse over new worker calls. Measure recovery work repeated and duplicate-run prevention, not merely how quickly a lease file disappears.
unverified: Power loss, network filesystems and Windows locks require actual platform tests; POSIX mocks are not proof of those guarantees.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated model calls; tests listed here are implementation obligations, not claimed passes.
